successCriteria.description: The service interface declares all seven operations with the specified async signatures: lookup by id (returns Employee | null), lookup by employee number (returns Employee | null), subordinates by manager id (returns Employee[]), all employees (returns Employee[]), create (input omits id/createdAt/updatedAt/deletedAt, returns Employee), update (id + partial, returns Employee | null), and terminate (id, returns void).

The service class implements the interface and, for every read/create/update operation, delegates to the injected repository, returning the repository's result unchanged and propagating repository errors without swallowing or wrapping them.

terminateEmployee sets employmentStatus to 'TERMINATED' and terminationDate to the current time via the repository update, then calls softDelete — update is invoked BEFORE softDelete so the status/terminationDate write is not lost to the deleted_at filter.

The module barrel re-exports the service interface and the service class alongside the existing model and repository exports, so downstream modules can consume IEmployeeService through the public entry point.

Unit tests with a mocked repository verify, for each operation, that the service calls the repository with the correct arguments and returns its result; for terminateEmployee they assert update is called with employmentStatus 'TERMINATED' and a Date terminationDate before softDelete is called; and that repository errors propagate unchanged (mockRejectedValueOnce → rejects.toThrow).
The phase compiles under strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict null checks) and the Jest suite passes with no failing tests.

constraints: The service must not access the database directly — all persistence goes through the injected IEmployeeRepository (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository).
The service interface file must import only the Employee model type (no repository or other module imports), mirroring the established leave-policy service-interface pattern.
The service class must inject only IEmployeeRepository via its constructor — no other dependencies (no audit repository, no notification service) are introduced in this phase.

terminateEmployee must call repository.update before repository.softDelete; reversing the order would cause the update (which filters WHERE deleted_at IS NULL) to match no rows and silently drop the status/terminationDate write.
The service must not write audit records for terminateEmployee in this phase; GP-002 audit compliance is deferred per the task scope and the established leave-policy service precedent.
No use of any — use unknown with type guards where dynamic typing is needed (no-any constraint).
The test file must use the .spec.ts extension and live under tests/unit/modules/employee/, mirroring the sibling employee.repository.spec.ts and the leave-policy service test.
outOfScope: Audit record writing for terminateEmployee or any other service operation (GP-002 compliance deferred to a later phase).
Input validation at API boundaries (GP-003) — no controller/routes layer in this phase; the service receives already-typed arguments.
RBAC enforcement (GP-005) — no HTTP surface in this phase; authorization is a controller/middleware concern.
Transaction wrapping of the update-then-softDelete sequence in terminateEmployee — the repository methods are independent calls; transactional orchestration is not part of this service-layer phase.
Notification emission on employee termination — the notification module is built in a later phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: Termination is a terminal lifecycle transition: terminateEmployee must move employmentStatus to 'TERMINATED' and set terminationDate to a non-null current timestamp before the record is soft-deleted; an employee cannot be terminated without both fields being persisted.

Soft-deletion (deletedAt set) must only occur after the termination status fields are written, because the repository's update path excludes rows where deleted_at IS NOT NULL — the ordering preserves the status/terminationDate write.

The service is a pure delegation layer over IEmployeeRepository for all read/create/update operations — it must not mutate, filter, or synthesize Employee data beyond the terminateEmployee status/terminationDate assignment.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Delegates to repository.findById; returns Employee | null; propagates repository errors unchanged.
Delegates to repository.findByEmployeeNumber; returns Employee | null; propagates repository errors unchanged.
Delegates to repository.findByManagerId; returns Employee[] (empty when none); propagates repository errors unchanged.
Delegates to repository.findAll; returns Employee[] (empty when none); propagates repository errors unchanged.
Delegates to repository.create with the provided data (omitting id/createdAt/updatedAt/deletedAt); returns the persisted Employee; propagates unique-constraint and other repository errors unchanged.
Delegates to repository.update; returns the updated Employee or null when no non-deleted row matches; propagates repository errors unchanged.

Calls repository.update with employmentStatus 'TERMINATED' and terminationDate = now, then calls repository.softDelete; resolves void on success; propagates repository errors unchanged (an update failure must not trigger softDelete).

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The service interface and class must import and operate on the exact Employee type defined in employee.model.ts — do not redefine or narrow the entity shape; the create input must omit precisely id, createdAt, updatedAt, and deletedAt.

The service must delegate to the existing IEmployeeRepository method set (findById, findByEmployeeNumber, findByManagerId, findAll, create, update, softDelete) without adding or assuming repository methods; terminateEmployee must compose update then softDelete from this exact set.

The employee service interface file must follow the leave-policy service-interface pattern: import only the model type, export the service interface with async method signatures, no repository import.

The employee service class must follow the leave-policy service class pattern: constructor takes a private readonly repository typed as the repository interface, implements the service interface, and each method delegates directly to the repository.
The employee barrel must add the service interface and class exports in the same ordering convention as the leave-policy barrel (model, repository, service interface, service class).

The employee service test must mirror the leave-policy service test structure: a jest.Mocked<IEmployeeRepository> built in beforeEach, a makeEmployee() factory helper, delegation assertions (correct args + returned value), and error-propagation assertions (mockRejectedValueOnce → rejects.toThrow).

integrationPoints.why: The service consumes the repository interface as its sole dependency; all persistence operations flow through it.
Downstream phases (Phase 10 leave-request orchestration) consume IEmployeeService and EmployeeService exclusively through the public barrel entry point per the module-boundary rule.
The employee service must structurally match the leave-policy service precedent so the codebase has one consistent service-layer shape.
